old_caption: The video showcases a festive scene at night, featuring a house adorned with an elaborate Christmas light display. The house is decorated with strings of lights, creating a warm and inviting glow. Various holiday-themed decorations, including Santa Claus figures, reindeer, snowmen, and candy canes, are scattered throughout the yard. The front porch is illuminated by additional lights, and a large star is prominently displayed on top of the roof. The camera pans slowly from left to right, capturing the intricate details of the decorations. The background remains dark, emphasizing the brightness of the lights and the festive atmosphere. The overall scene is vibrant and cheerful, reflecting the joyous spirit of the holiday season.

caption: The video showcases a single-story house at night, blanketed in Christmas lights: icicle strands trace the roofline, star outlines and Santa figures sit on top, the garage glows pink, and the yard holds a wire reindeer, candy-cane poles and gingerbread houses. Throughout the clip the camera eases back in a widening, the roofline stars shifting toward center while the green-lit tree at the left and the waving snowman at the right edge stay in view. Meanwhile the display animates continuously, the wheel light shifting pattern and the central props flickering between hues. These changes run independently of the camera shift, the reindeer outline holding steady as the wheel light flips color, while the icicle twinkle persists throughout without either motion reaching a finished state.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

draft_caption: The video showcases a single-story house at night, blanketed in Christmas lights: icicle strands trace the roofline, star outlines and Santa figures sit on top, the garage glows pink, and the yard holds a wire reindeer, candy-cane poles and gingerbread houses. Throughout the clip the camera performs a slow lateral drive-by, near props drifting rightward against the nearly fixed roofline stars, sliding the framing left to reveal a green-lit tree and candy-striped figures while the right-edge snowman exits view. Meanwhile the display animates continuously, the central tree cycling green, red and white and the wheel light shifting pattern. These changes run independently of the camera shift, the reindeer outline staying white as the tree flips hue, while the icicle twinkle persists throughout without either motion reaching a finished state.

review_issues.quote: the camera performs a slow lateral drive-by, near props drifting rightward against the nearly fixed roofline stars, sliding the framing left to reveal a green-lit tree and candy-striped figures while the right-edge snowman exits view.
review_issues.problem: The green-lit tree and the candy-cane poles are already visible in the first frame, and the waving snowman on the right edge remains fully in view through the last frame; the camera change is a subtle widening/zoom-out (off-center stars drift toward center), not a leftward slide that reveals new props or pushes the snowman out.

review_issues.quote: the central tree cycling green, red and white
review_issues.problem: The central green tree holds its green hue across the clip; the obvious color cycling occurs in the pinwheel/wheel light and the surrounding props, not in that tree.
